Closest recent match: [MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns multiple attribute-aware user/item representations and matches them attribute-wise, addressing information lost when all semantics collapse into one vector. It uses pretrained language models, so its results do not establish effectiveness for training text encoders from scratch. [AttrFormer (KDD 2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3690624.3709267) models attributes as explicit relations, targeting interference between attribute signals. Both motivate distinguishing specific textual cues from broad semantic similarity; neither establishes the exact constrained BERT4Rec setup requested.

An older, directly compatible reference is [NOVA-BERT (2021)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16549): side information guides attention queries/keys while values preserve item-ID representations. Its experiments found naive embedding fusion could provide little benefit or hurt performance. A proposed adaptation—not a verified literature result—is a small, randomly initialized title/description token encoder, jointly trained within one BERT4Rec network, with field-specific projections and gated attention guidance. Retain item IDs for discrimination; derive features only from available text, without inventing structured attributes.

Leakage safeguard follows [BERT4Rec’s Cloze objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690): when hiding a target interaction, hide its ID and every associated text feature at that position. Append a metadata-free reserved mask at inference and read its final nonpadding position. Candidate text may enter the shared candidate representation consistently for every candidate, without entering the history as the known answer. Use one jointly trained scoring network/checkpoint per category; assess any benefit through the fixed macro validation HR@10.
